## 3. Acquire the rates while preserving relative accuracy

Syndrome-correlation calibration is established prior work, including Spitz and colleagues and the more general experimental treatment by Remm and colleagues. The useful additional step here is to propagate calibration error into **uniform multiplicative bounds on every logical-class weight**. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}

Let
\[
t_e=1-2p_e,\qquad
\mu_v=\mathbb E(-1)^{s_v}.
\]
For a unique interior edge \(e=uv\), independence gives
\[
\mu_v=\prod_{e\ni v}t_e,
\qquad
\mu_{uv}:=\mathbb E(-1)^{s_u+s_v}
=\frac{\mu_u\mu_v}{t_e^2}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{t_e=\sqrt{\frac{\mu_u\mu_v}{\mu_{uv}}}.}
\tag{8}
\]

A boundary-edge factor follows by dividing \(\mu_v\) by the recovered interior factors.

There is a genuine identifiability boundary: if one detector adjoins both unobserved rough components, its observations can identify only the product of those boundary factors. Different logical risks can then produce identical syndrome data. Ordinary separated patches of distance at least three avoid this two-edge logical path. Parallel mechanisms may be merged only when their detector incidence and logical effect agree.

Let the detector degree be at most \(\Delta\), and put
\[
a=(1-2p_{\max})^{2\Delta}.
\]
All required moments are at least \(a\). If their simultaneous estimation error is at most \(\xi\le a/2\), logarithmic propagation, clipping to the promised rate interval, and budgeted rational rounding give
\[
\Gamma:=
\sum_e\left|\log\frac{\widehat q_e}{q_e}\right|
\le
\frac{6m\Delta\,\xi}{a p_{\min}}
+\text{rounding allowance}.
\tag{9}
\]

Therefore, simultaneously for **every** history and syndrome,
\[
e^{-\Gamma}\prod_e q_e^{z_e}
\le
\prod_e\widehat q_e^{z_e}
\le
e^\Gamma\prod_e q_e^{z_e},
\]
and thus
\[
\boxed{
e^{-\Gamma}Z_h(s)
\le \widehat Z_h^{\,\mathrm{model}}(s)
\le e^\Gamma Z_h(s).
}
\tag{10}
\]

No factor \(1/\Pr(s)\) appears. Rare conditioning remains controlled because the bound holds before conditioning, pointwise on histories.

A sufficient calibration budget is
\[
K=
O\!\left(
\frac{m^2\Delta^2}
{a^2p_{\min}^2\varepsilon^2}
\log\frac{m}{\delta_{\mathrm{cal}}}
\right)
\tag{11}
\]
independent repetitions, each producing \(O(m)\) detector bits.

This is polynomial at fixed physical rate bounds and bounded degree. It is polynomial in \(p_{\min}^{-1}\), **not merely its bit length**. Extremely

### Executed construction checks

I executed exact checks of all 28 local parity signatures, 40 rational \(T\)-join/matching partition identities, integer-weight gadgets for weights \(1\) through \(64\), and a complete rational-to-unweighted identity. A separate enumeration of 256 fault histories recovered all eight edge rates from syndrome moments and checked the risk comparison across all 16 detector records.

These verify finite construction identities. **The general FPRAS was not implemented or benchmarked.**
